detailZh: 阿塞拜疆大奖赛：迈凯伦确认MCL40赛车再度升级，并预测在巴库将与对手展开四方争夺胜利的较量
迈凯伦近期状态强劲，兰多·诺里斯在过去四轮比赛中夺得三次杆位和两场分站冠军；从周四起通过天空体育F1频道观看阿塞拜疆大奖赛的每一节练习赛和排位赛直播，正赛将于周六中午12点举行
兰多·诺里斯表示，由于错过了一次关键的安全车虚拟状态下的进站，导致他丢掉了领先位置，他的迈凯伦车队当时'反应太慢了'
迈凯伦已确认他们将在本周末的阿塞拜疆大奖赛带来更多升级件，他们预计将与梅赛德斯、法拉利和红牛展开四方争夺胜利的战斗。
在赛季前10场大奖赛未能夺冠之后，这支卫冕车队冠军已经找回状态，兰多·诺里斯在过去四场比赛中拿下三个杆位，上一站在马德里只是因为虚拟安全车出现的不巧时机而错失了第三个分站冠军。
迈凯伦再一次展现了研发方面的实力，持续为MCL40带来的升级件在将他们重新推回争冠行列中发挥了重要作用。

车队的官方前瞻介绍提到，本周末在巴库举行的比赛将在周六而非通常的周日时段进行，车队将为本站带来新的零部件，并且他们的旋转式"H-翼"（H-Wing）在马德里站未使用之后，将重新装回赛车上。
诺里斯在西班牙大奖赛中因一连串不幸事件失去了领先位置：先是在虚拟安全车期间错过了进站时机，随后一次进站又非常缓慢
车队表示：“作为车队在2026赛季持续推进旅程的一部分，车队将为本届巴库大奖赛带来一套升级套件，旨在提升MCL40的空气动力学性能。”
“此外，在蒙扎首次亮相的H翼将重新投入使用，在这条赛道上，减少风阻可能成为一个关键因素。”
“按照本赛季此前几场比赛的一贯做法，所有新部件都将在练习赛中逐一评估，之后车队才会就MCL40在本周末排位赛和大奖赛的调校做出最终决定。”
迈凯伦技术总监兼首席设计师罗布·马歇尔解释说，尽管车队的夺冠希望已经非常渺茫——基米·安东内利统治着车手总冠军，他所在的梅赛德斯车队在车队积分榜上也遥遥领先——但车队仍热衷于继续推进研发工作。
观看诺里斯以为自己跑砸了那一圈、结果却为西班牙大奖赛拿下杆位的时刻
“由于下赛季规则保持延续性，而且前方竞争对手之间的差距如此接近，我们继续研发赛车的动力依然很高，”马歇尔说。
“我们必须在这一点与明年赛车的工作之间取得平衡，但我们当前的重点是提升更多性能，并在2026年争取更多胜利，同时把学到的所有经验延续下去。”
巴库赛道拥有F1赛历中最长的直道，同时还有多个慢速弯角，马歇尔预计这将带来一场颇具观赏性的顶尖车队之间的竞争。
“巴库将在截然不同的特性范围内对MCL40进行又一次宝贵的检验，”马歇尔补充道。
诺里斯对摩纳哥大奖赛将于2027年举办冲刺赛的消息作出回应
“能量管理和动力输出将尤为重要，轮胎和刹车的管理也同样关键，因为赛车经过长直道后到达一号弯时这些区域温度相对较低。
“在运营层面，狭窄的街道赛道几乎没有容错空间。一个小失误就可能导致高昂的维修成本、损失赛道时间，以及资源从提升性能上被转移，因此整个周末都必须保持信心、精准和严格执行。”
"我们预计前四名车队中的任何一支都有能力在巴库夺冠，同时追赶集团也在逐渐逼近，我们希望自己能牢牢站在前列的争夺之中。"

detailEn: Azerbaijan GP: McLaren predict four-way battle for victory with rivals in Baku after confirming more upgrades to MCL40

McLaren have shown strong recent form with Lando Norris claiming three pole positions and two race victories across the last four rounds; watch every session of the Azerbaijan GP from Thursday live on Sky Sports F1, with the race on Saturday at 12pm
Lando Norris says his McLaren team 'were too quick' after missing out on a crucial VSC pit stop that cost him race lead
McLaren have confirmed they will bring more upgrades to this weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, where they are expecting a four-way battle for victory with Mercedes, Ferrari and Red Bull.

After failing to claim a victory in the first 10 grands prix of the season, the reigning constructors' champions have come into form, with Lando Norris claiming three pole positions at the last four races and only being denied a third win by the unfortunate timing of a virtual safety car last time out in Madrid.
McLaren have once more exhibited strength in development, with regular upgrades brought to the MCL40 having played a significant part in catapulting them back into contention for victories.

The team's official preview for this weekend's race in Baku, which takes place on Saturday rather than the usual Sunday slot, revealed there will be new parts, and that their rotating 'H-Wing' will return to the car after not being used in Madrid.
Norris lost the lead of the Spanish GP after an unlucky sequence of events which saw a missed a pit-stop opportunity under a VSC, followed by a very slow stop
"As part of the team's continued journey throughout the 2026 season, the team will bring to Baku a set of upgrades aimed to improve the aerodynamic performance of the MCL40," the team said.
"Additionally the H-Wing, that debuted in Monza, will be back in action on a track where the drag reduction can be a factor.

"As has been the approach in previous races this season, all new parts will be evaluated throughout practice before the team makes final decisions regarding the MCL40's Qualifying and Grand Prix setup for the weekend."

McLaren chief technical officer and chief designer Rob Marshall explained the team are keen to continue their development push despite their title hopes being extremely thin, with Kimi Antonelli dominating the Drivers' Championship and his Mercedes team well clear in the constructors' standings.
Watch the moment Norris thought he messed up his lap, which turned out to put him on the pole for the Spanish Grand Prix
"With regulatory continuity into next season and the competition at the front so close, our motivation to keep developing the car remains high," Marshall said.
"We must balance that with work on next year's car, but our immediate focus is on delivering more performance and fighting for more victories in 2026, while carrying forward everything we learn."

The Baku circuit, which features the longest straight on the F1 calendar alongside several slow corners, creates a challenge that Marshall expects to create entertaining competition between the top teams.
"Baku will provide another valuable test of the MCL40 across a very different range of characteristics," Marshall added.
Norris reacts to the news that the Monaco Grand Prix will be a Sprint race in 2027
"Energy management and deployment will be particularly important, as will tyre and brake management with the cars arriving at Turn 1 after the long straight with these areas relatively cold.

"Operationally, there is very little margin for error on a tight street circuit. A small mistake can lead to significant repairs, lost track time and resources being diverted away from performance, so confidence, precision and disciplined execution will be essential throughout the weekend.
"We expect any of the top four teams to be capable of winning in Baku, with the chasing pack also getting closer, and we hope to be firmly in the fight at the front."

detailEn: United States GP: Lewis Hamilton fastest from Max Verstappen in final practice ahead of Qualifying in Austin

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton outpaced Red Bull's Max Verstappen in final practice in Austin with Friday's pace-setter Charles Leclerc in third; watch every United States GP session live on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 10pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday
Lewis Hamilton claims the fastest lap from Max Verstappen in final practice at the United States Grand Prix
Lewis Hamilton topped final practice from Max Verstappen at the United States Grand Prix to set up a tantalising qualifying in Austin.
Hamilton was 0.168s quicker than Verstappen as Ferrari and Red Bull look set to fight for pole position and victory for a second consecutive weekend.
Charles Leclerc topped both of Friday's sessions and had set the quickest time in final practice by one tenth from Hamilton, only for it to be deleted due to track limits.

Track limits is set to be a major issue for the drivers in qualifying, which takes place at 10pm UK time later on Saturday (build-up from 8.30pm live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event) due to the tarmac run-off areas and the drivers keen to use every bit of track to gain lap time.

Leclerc still finished the session in third, ahead of championship leader Kimi Antonelli whose chances of becoming the youngest world champion look extremely difficult, given he must first win the Grand Prix to give himself an opportunity, and Mercedes are a tad off the pace.
Antonelli was three tenths behind Hamilton's pace-setting time with his Mercedes team-mate George Russell in fifth at nearly half a second down.

McLaren's Lando Norris was eighth but would have been in the top five had his best lap not been deleted for track limit, while Oscar Piastri was sixth and Audi's Nico Hulkenberg impressing in seventh.
